# First, let's observe visual and measure block1, block2, block3 to see which is red, green, blue, and get visual provenance handles.
res_vis = primitives.call(
    name="observe_robotwin2_visual",
    camera_name="head_camera",
    prompt="observe blocks",
    query="blocks",
)
print("vis ok:", res_vis.ok)
if res_vis.ok:
    print("handles:", res_vis.output.get("evidence_handles"))

for b in ["block1", "block2", "block3"]:
    res_m = primitives.call(
        name="measure_robotwin2_actor_visual",
        actor_label=b,
        camera_name="head_camera",
        depth_scale=1.0,
        max_points=500,
        prompt=f"measure {b}",
    )
    print(b, "ok:", res_m.ok)
    if res_m.ok:
        out = res_m.output
        print(
            b,
            "pose:",
            out.get("pose_world") or out.get("center_world") or out.get("bbox_world"),
            "rgb:",
            out.get("mean_rgb"),
            "handles:",
            out.get("evidence_handles"),
            "keys:",
            list(out.keys()),
        )

    for pt in ["contact", "functional", "target", "orientation"]:
        res_pt = primitives.call(
            name="inspect_robotwin2_actor_points", actor_name=b, point_type=pt
        )
        if res_pt.ok:
            print(b, pt, res_pt.output)

steps.code:
# Look at the image! The right gripper is pointing horizontally instead of straight down!
# Why? Because in RoboTwin2:
# get_arm_pose() / endpose returns the gripper pose in SAPIEN convention, OR contact points are in SAPIEN convention, whereas take_action(action_type='ee') or top_down_plan converts or doesn't convert!
# Let's check what probe_robotwin2_motion_plan returns RIGHT NOW for the current right arm pose and for the 4 contact points of block1!
rp_curr = primitives.call(
    name="probe_robotwin2_motion_plan", arm_tag="right", evidence_handles=handles
)
print("curr pose:", rp_curr.output.get("current_pose"))
for i, c in enumerate(b1_contacts):
    rp = primitives.call(
        name="probe_robotwin2_motion_plan",
        arm_tag="right",
        evidence_handles=handles,
        target_pose=[c[0], c[1], c[2] + 0.08] + c[3:],
    )
    print("b1 contact", i, rp.output.get("path_summary"))

# Also let's test what quaternion makes the gripper point straight down in take_action(action_type='ee')!
# Look at when we sent pre1 = [0.1688, 0.0114, 0.845, 0.7056, 0.7056, -0.045, -0.045]:
# Resulting right_arm pose_world was: [0.1550, 0.0989, 0.8384, 0.7508, 0.6509, 0.0665, 0.0900]
# And in the image, the gripper is pointing along +Y (horizontally forward) with its camera on top!
# Wait: at initial state, right_endpose was:
# [0.3064, -0.3128, 0.9410, 0.70356, -7e-6, -3.8e-6, 0.71063]
